what_matters.head: Intel fell 28.6% on Friday, about 7.5 times its usual daily move, and the chip fund fell 8.2%, about 3.5 times usual.
what_matters.detail: CNBC called it Intel's worst day since the 1970s. Its Q4 forecast of $15–16B revenue and 25 cents a share was below the $17.1B and 43 cents analysts expected (LSEG), and its finance chief said the PC slowdown will last at least through the first half of next year. AMD fell 10.9%, Sandisk 13.5%, TSMC 6.0%, ASML 6.5%, Broadcom 5.5% and Nvidia 4.2%. Investopedia said chip stocks fell across the board. Yahoo Finance counts about $5 trillion of market value lost by the biggest AI and chip stocks since 6 Oct, while the other 625 large US stocks in its count gained about $1.3 trillion.

what_matters.head: Tower reports tonight at about 20:00 SGT, Palantir after Monday's New York close (Tue 05:05 SGT) and AMD after Tuesday's (Wed 05:05 SGT).
what_matters.detail: Tower's forecast is $520M ± 5% for Q3. Palantir forecast $2.160–2.164B for Q3; analysts expect about $2.2B. AMD forecast $13.0B ± $300M at about 56% gross margin; analysts expect about $13.1B, and options trading implies a move of about ±8.9% either way by 4 Nov.

what_matters.head: OCBC was down 3.5% and DBS 2.4% by 12:05 SGT, each about 2.5 times its usual daily move, on volume about 3–4 times usual for this time of day.
what_matters.detail: No reported cause found. All three banks report this week: UOB's trading update on Wednesday, DBS on Thursday and OCBC on Friday (dates the banks call indicative or post without a time).

after_data.text: Yahoo Finance reported that US stock futures opened higher, led by the Nasdaq 100. Not in Friday's US prices.

WTI was at $100.80 at the 12:05 SGT run, 3.2% below Friday's settlement. Reuters (via the Business Times) tied the early fall to a third straight day of talks between Iranian and Qatari officials on ending the war on Iran. OPEC+ kept its December output targets unchanged (Yahoo Finance).

OCBC's insurer posted Q3 net profit of S$102.9M, down 72% from a year earlier, on weaker investment valuations and a one-off loss from selling part of its Indonesian unit to OCBC Indonesia. OCBC owns 93.7% of Great Eastern. No article ties OCBC's fall to it.

recent.headline: Intel fell 28.6% on Friday, about 7.5 times its usual daily move, and the chip fund fell 8.2%, about 3.5 times usual.
Alphabet fell 12.3% on Thursday, about 8 times its usual daily move, on volume 3.6 times normal. It was the first full session after its Q3 results.
Alphabet fell 9.8% in after-hours trading after its profit came in below forecasts. Microsoft rose 2.9% after hours on faster cloud growth. Neither move is in Wednesday's US prices.
SK Hynix's third-quarter revenue passed 100 trillion won for the first time, and operating profit beat forecasts. By 12:05 SGT its shares were up 10.5%, 2.2× their usual day.
Bloom Energy fell 11.2% on Friday, 2.2× its usual day, even though its third-quarter results beat forecasts and it raised its 2026 revenue forecast.
